text.p: Note: The news on Wednesday evening that President Boris Yeltsin had been taken to hospital came too late for Thursday's morning newspapers.
- Russia plans to restart construction work on the unfinished BAM railway line linking Europe to the Far East.
- Crew members of the wrecked tanker Nakhodka which broke into two in high seas off Japan a week ago return to Russia on Thursday amid doubts as to what caused the disaster.
- Everyone will suffer from the soon-to-be-introduced $10 border tax.
- The Defence Ministry and the Defence Council clash over the army reform.
- Foreign Minister Evgeny Primakov has managed to avoid making mistakes during his first year in office and preserved all the gains he inherited from his predecessor.
- The Kremlin seems to be dissatisfied with Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and the latter could come under fire at the next meeting of the Defence Council.
- President Yeltsin orders the Foreign Ministry to take measures to respond to NATO's planned eastwards expansion.
- The Kremlin chimes played a special Christmas melody on January 7, Orthodox Christmas day, for the first time since 1917.
